In the RAG paper, the difference between the two models lies in how they treat the retrieved documents as latent variables to marginalize and produce the output text [rag_lewis_2020.pdf p. 3]:

* **RAG-Sequence Model:** This model uses the *same* retrieved document to generate the complete target sequence [rag_lewis_2020.pdf p. 3]. It treats the retrieved document as a single latent variable that is marginalized using a top-$K$ approximation to get the sequence-to-sequence probability $p(y|x)$ [rag_lewis_2020.pdf p. 3].
* **RAG-Token Model:** This model can draw a *different* latent document for each target token [rag_lewis_2020.pdf p. 3]. This allows the generator to choose content from multiple different documents when producing an answer [rag_lewis_2020.pdf p. 3]. Concretely, the generator produces a distribution for the next output token for each retrieved document before marginalizing, and then repeats the process for each subsequent output token [rag_lewis_2020.pdf p. 3].

The base Transformer uses **8** parallel attention layers, or heads ($h = 8$) [attention_is_all_you_need.pdf p. 5, p. 9]. 

The dimension of each key, value, and query head is $d_k = d_v = 64$ (calculated as $d_{\text{model}} / h = 512 / 8 = 64$) [attention_is_all_you_need.pdf p. 5, p. 9].
